items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Was the closest you got the band that you and Frank Wess led not that long ago, was that over in Japan?

ctx.x: No. Then I never had the pleasure of having even a small band to travel in Europe with me, I always travelled by myself. My name wasn’t big enough to demand the kind of money that I could say, well, for my band, I want to take over there.
Was the closest you got the band that you and Frank Wess led not that long ago, was that over in Japan?
Yeah, Japan. We got the band together just for that engagement and after that when we got back to America, everybody went their own way.

items.title: Frank Wess — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So you know like, Harry Edison, he’s like, “You’ve already missed two gigs while I was listening to that message!”

ctx.x: You have to describe what the message is.

Well, it’s just…I tried to cover all the things that I have to listen to all the time. Somebody’s always trying to give you a story about this or that, so I just said, “Hi there, how are you doing? You’re not going to believe this. I was just thinking about you. You must be physic; it’s so nice to have sensitive friends. If your call pertains to me doing a benefit for one of the, so-called, non-profit organizations by about my performance with one of the trendy necrophilia ensembles, I suggest you call my manager…
